body:
here's an overview of what changed for cx_Oracle:

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_2/changelog/migration_12.html#major-refactor-to-cx-oracle-dialect-typing-system

the code at work here is likely at https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/master/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/oracle/cx_oracle.py#L900

can you attempt to set coerce_to_decimal=False on create_engine?  see https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_2/dialects/oracle.html#cx-oracle-numeric for details on this feature.

so ill have to report upstream issues with cx_oracle which is waht usually happens here.   When the type is sent with precision 19 and scale 0, that means it's an integer, so SQLAlchemy uses cx_Oracle's API to treat this as cx_Oracle.NATIVE_INT.  that's wahts failing for starters.
im also not getting that result for 32 bit integer underflow, it matches for me...

issue.title: more confusion about binding NATIVE_INT

repository.name: python-cx_Oracle
repository.description: Obsolete Python interface to Oracle Database, now superseded by python-oracledb

body: welp I'll just stick "int" in there for now, seems to work fine.    but I can only reproduce the error you were getting, not the part where the integer underflow doesnt match.   The patch coming in should likely improve things at least.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Don't use cx_Oracle.NATIVE_INT in output type handlers** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1107

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_2** branch:

**Don't use cx_Oracle.NATIVE_INT in output type handlers** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1108
